title: AI fire alert precedes the first 911 call near Grass Valley
date_precision: Day and local alert time explicitly reported.
location: Near Grass Valley, California, United States
system: ALERTCalifornia camera network and DigitalPath/CAL FIRE fire-detection AI.
observed_outcome: AI alerted at 5:19 a.m. Firefighters were on scene before the first 911 call at 6:01 a.m. The fire remained under a quarter acre.
ai_contribution: Detected a possible ignition in the Wolf Mountain 1 camera feed and alerted firefighters.
human_contribution: The program uses trained watchstanders to confirm detections. Firefighters responded and contained this fire.
evidence_type: First-party program report. No independent causal evaluation.
evidence_supports: The university operating the camera program reports the alert, first-call times, and final containment.
limitations: Earlier notification and containment are observed. A larger fire, specific losses, or casualties avoided are not established. The comparison is with the first 911 call, not every possible detection route.
tradeoffs: No event-specific adverse effects are reported. False alarms, response costs, and surveillance effects are not evaluated.
replication_hypothesis: Test whether camera coverage, human confirmation, reliable dispatch, and available crews produce earlier effective responses elsewhere.
beneficiaries: Emergency responders received earlier notification. Nearby residents and property were intended downstream beneficiaries, but specific losses avoided are unmeasured.

sources.title: ALERTCalifornia and CAL FIRE's Fire Detection AI Program Named One of TIME's Best Inventions of 2023

benefit_summary: An AI fire alert reached firefighters before the first 911 call. Crews were already on scene when that call arrived.
stakeholder_detail: Earlier notification to firefighters is the reported operational benefit. Nearby residents are intended beneficiaries, but an individual or community welfare improvement is not measured.

evidence_basis.evidence_design: Single-episode report with alert and call times
evidence_basis.reported_by: UC San Diego, a partner in the ALERTCalifornia program
evidence_basis.outcome_documentation: Reports a 5:19 a.m. AI alert, the first 911 call at 6:01 a.m., crews already on scene, and containment below a quarter acre.
evidence_basis.verification_limit: The comparator is the first 911 call. No independent causal evaluation establishes response time without AI or losses avoided.

ai_attribution: The source explicitly attributes the camera alert to AI. Human confirmation and firefighting remain essential parts of the response.
editorial_classification_note: Include as a documented operational benefit, not as proven prevention. Keep the measured alert advantage separate from unmeasured downstream community benefits.
